claims.summary: If a matching is (L,alpha)-good in coordinate j with alpha in (0,infinity), then for every t>=0 at most 2N e^(-t) pairs have |X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)| >= L sqrt(log N/N) t^(1/alpha); hence for every a,delta,beta>0, if more than N (log N)^(-a) pairs have |X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)| >= delta (log N)^(1/2+beta)/sqrt N, the matching is not (L,alpha)-good in coordinate j for N >= N_0(a,delta,beta,L,alpha).
claims.assessment: Working proof: Markov's inequality on the exponential sum, at t=(delta/L)^alpha (log N)^(alpha beta), which exceeds a log log N + log 2 for large N.
claims.rationale: The level-count form of the exponential condition that refutations of constructions use.

claims.summary: For alpha_1,alpha_2 in (0,infinity], square cells of side s=s_N -> 0 with s sqrt N >= delta (log N)^(1/2+gamma) (delta,gamma>0 fixed), X,Y independent uniform samples: for each fixed measurable rule that, in each cell with excess z(u)>0, chooses z(u) of its X points by cell memberships and labels only and matches them to Y points outside the cell, and every L, with probability tending to one the matching fails to be (L,alpha_j)-good in some coordinate j. In particular the matching of [C5] (Ouimet, solution of Talagrand's Problem 5.3) fails the (4,4) condition for every L.
claims.assessment: Working proof: McDiarmid gives sqrt N/(8s) exits; conditional on memberships and labels the exits are uniform in their cells, a quarter lie at depth s/4 and move at least s/4 in some coordinate; the level count of lem:level-count-consequence at t=(s sqrt N/(4L sqrt log N))^alpha_j excludes goodness. [C5]'s excess is its largest-label points (its Section 2.5), each paired into a side-neighbouring cell (Section 2.6).
claims.rationale: Excludes the known simultaneous AKT/Leighton-Shor construction at (4,4) and shows that the points leaving a coarse cell must be chosen by position.
claims.next_action: Test a position-aware repair: exits chosen nearest the side they leave through, recursively at dyadic scales, against the level counts 2N e^(-t).

relationships: The count at every level; that lemma's maximum bound is its top level, its sum bound is not implied.
Excludes a class of constructions, [C5]'s included, at (4,4) and at every pair with beta>0.
Maximal displacements alone cannot refute a pair of the curve; this obstruction uses level counts of one construction class.
